actions.description: Capture a single image from a named camera with a declared resolution and exposure and return an image artifact reference.

inputs.description: Select one declared image source; each capture is independent.
inputs.name: camera

actions.name: capture_image

facts.text: README says Unreal Engine 4 provides imagery and depth sensor data.
The listener initializes a ROS 1 node named 'ue4_bridge' with rospy.init_node and anonymous=True.
The bridge imports its deployment config from UNREAL_PROXY_PATH and reads config.zmq_pub_unreal_proxy and config.topic_unreal_drone_rgb_camera.
The shipped demo config sets topic_unreal_drone_rgb_camera to b'rgb_camera_%d'.
The bridge formats the camera topic template with index 0 and subscribes on its ZMQ socket to that name plus the literal suffixes b'down' and b'depth'.
For a non-depth ZMQ topic not yet in its publisher map the bridge creates a sensor_msgs/Image publisher on the same relative topic with queue_size 2.
For a non-depth topic the bridge reshapes the uint8 payload to the received shape and publishes it with cv2_to_imgmsg as a bgr8 sensor_msgs/Image without setting its header.

For a depth ZMQ topic not yet in its publisher map the bridge creates sensor_msgs/Image publishers on <topic>_rgb8 and <topic>_range_mm and a sensor_msgs/CameraInfo publisher on <topic>_cam_info, each with queue_size 2.

For a depth topic the bridge reads the A channel of the float16 RGBA payload as depth in centimetres, maps the 65504 error sample to zero, multiplies by 10 to millimetres, casts to uint16 and publishes a mono16 sensor_msgs/Image with frame_id camera_depth on <topic>_range_mm.
The bridge creates the publishers of a ZMQ topic only when the first message on that topic arrives.
The depth CameraInfo sets height 240 and width 320 as constants.
The shipped image_view launch remaps image to rgb_camera_0 and rgb_camera_0depth_range_mm.
The shipped RGB-D SLAM node subscribes to /rgb_camera_0depth_rgb8 and /rgb_camera_0depth_range_mm as sensor_msgs::Image.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned image frames with no renderer or physics step; the same request returns the same placeholder bytes, which is not trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free protocol transport: it answers the two declared image subscriptions and runs no UE4 renderer, ZMQ proxy, drone physics or ROS graph
the fake returns a 2x2 placeholder frame; the deployment's UE4 render-target size is configured outside the clone and is not a fixed device bound
depth samples in the fake are placeholders; the clone's conversion yields millimetre integers, but the driver preserves the mono16 samples and makes no calibration or accuracy claim
the clone multiplies the float16 centimetre depth by 10 before the uint16 cast (ue4_bridge.py:69-72); a sample outside that representable range is not repaired by the bridge or by this driver
the bridge publishes the color stream without setting its header (empty frame_id, zero stamp; ue4_bridge.py:53-55), unlike the stamped depth stream; the fake mirrors the empty frame_id
the rgb_camera_0down stream, the CameraInfo topic and the ZMQ control channels are not exposed
the bridge creates its publishers lazily after the first ZMQ frame; a live subscription can time out until the UE4 proxy starts publishing
